title: Authorization and Least Privilege
summary: Reason about roles, permissions, scope, and separation of duties.
objectives: Identify excessive or missing permissions in synthetic cases.

vocab.def: Giving an identity only the access needed for an authorized responsibility.
A defined collection of responsibilities or permissions.
Dividing sensitive responsibilities so one person does not control every step.

sections.heading: Access has a purpose
sections.body: A contractor may need read access without administration. A former worker account may need disabling. Recommendations must stay within authorized administrative processes.

sections.heading: Review the model
sections.body: SHF review illustrates separation of duties: the learner submits evidence, while an authorized reviewer evaluates it. Membership alone is not review authority.

practice.prompt: A synthetic contractor role includes unnecessary administrator access. What is the safe recommendation?
practice.answer: Document the excess scope and request an authorized access review; do not change the account yourself.

criteria: Avoids unauthorized action and documents a recommendation

reflectionPrompt: What evidence would an authorized access reviewer need?
